subject: Hosted API — deletion timelines, backup retention & residency controls
messages:
From: Claire Moran <claire.moran@aquilahealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@aquilahealth.com
Date: 2027-03-14T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Hosted API — data location, deletion windows, and backup retention

Diego,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Our security team has a few follow-ups for the Hosted API piece before we can sign off on a pilot:

1) Primary question: if we elect to run under Redwood's Hosted API and pin our data to the us-east region, what is the default timeline from a customer-initiated deletion request to complete removal from live systems?
2) Are there any separate retention windows for backups/snapshot copies? If so, what guarantees or controls do you offer (e.g., can we request a shorter backup retention or an accelerated purge)?
3) How do cached prompt prefixes / KV cache entries get handled on deletion requests? Any possibility of residual artifacts in long-lived caches?
4) What evidence can Redwood provide after the deletion is complete (audit log entries, export of deletion event, signed attestation)?

We're mostly looking for concrete timelines, any configurable options for backup retention, and what the DPA/contract language looks like around deletions and legal holds.

Appreciate a concise FAQ-style response we can share with InfoSec.

- Claire
Claire Moran
Head of Platform Security
Aquila Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Moran <claire.moran@aquilahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data location, deletion windows, and backup retention

Claire — thanks for the clear questions. I captured these and looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Neha (security/product) to provide definitive answers and evidence. High-level answers below; Neha will follow with the technical details and links to the evidence we can provide.

Quick answers (summary):
- Live data deletion: We perform logical deletion from active stores within 48 hours of a verified request; physical removal from hot storage typically completes within 7 days.
- Backups & snapshots: Default backup retention is 90 days for hosted customers; shorter retention (30 days) can be requested in the contract for enterprise accounts or via an approved exception.
- Cache / KV: KV cache entries are soft-evicted on deletion; we run an asynchronous purge pipeline that clears related cache keys within 72 hours.
- Evidence: We can provide an audit event export with timestamps for the delete request and purge tasks, plus a signed DPA addendum confirming timelines.

I'll hand the thread to Neha for the technical/ops write-up and attachments we can share.

Best,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Moran <claire.moran@aquilahealth.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T12:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data location, deletion windows, and backup retention (technical details)

Claire — thanks for the questions. I'm Neha (Product Security). Below is a compact Q&A with specifics we can include in the DPA. I focused on Hosted API behavior for a us-east tenancy, but the timelines are the same across regions unless the customer requests a dedicated retention profile on Redwood Dedicated/Private.

Q1 — Live systems deletion timeline:
- Verified request received (authenticated API or signed support ticket): action created immediately.
- Logical delete from active databases + metadata flags: typically completed within 0–48 hours. Logical delete removes customer identifiers and marks documents/records as deleted (not returned by API).
- Physical sweep: background job compacts/zeroes/deletes storage segments; completes within 7 calendar days in normal operations. We quote 7 days as our practical maximum for hot-tier storage under normal conditions.

Q2 — Backups & snapshots:
- Default: 90-day retention for point-in-time backups and object-store snapshots. Backups are encrypted and stored with cross-region redundancy for disaster recovery (unless customer requests single-region).
- Shortening retention: For enterprise customers, we can contractually set backup retention to 30 days with an administrative change request and DPA addendum.
- Accelerated purge: We offer an expedited destruction workflow for documented compliance needs (e.g., data subject requests tied to regulated PHI). Expedited purges are executed within 72 hours of approval and require executed agreement (DPA amendment + JIRA ticket for ops).

Q3 — KV / inference caches:
- Inference KV caches and prefix caches operate on ephemeral stores attached to serving nodes. On deletion, we enqueue a cache invalidation event referencing hashed customer keys. Typical invalidation completes within 24–72 hours depending on cache TTL and active sessions.
- Note: If cached keys were exported to external logging or third-party observability tools, those exports follow the retention policy of that sink. We will include clarifying language in the DPA about third-party telemetry sinks.

Q4 — Evidence & auditables:
- We can deliver: (a) a CSV export of audit events showing the delete request ID, timestamps for logical delete and physical purge jobs; (b) S3-style object deletion manifests where applicable; (c) a signed attestation letter confirming the purge completion.
- Logs retention: Operational logs (request traces) are stored by default for 30 days; aggregated telemetry used for platform health is retained 90 days. Longer log retention is available as an add-on.

Q5 — Legal holds & exceptions:
- We will not purge data subject to an active legal hold. Legal hold overrides must be presented in writing and will be tracked through our legal intake process.

I've attached an excerpt of our DPA with the deletion clause highlighted and a retention matrix that maps artifact types (live DB, cache, backups, logs) to default timelines. I can also run a redline DPA showing the 30-day backup retention option if you want to see contract language.

Neha Kapoor
Product Security, Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — that level of detail is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before I share with legal:

1) For the "physical sweep within 7 days" — can you confirm whether that includes any encrypted cold backups (e.g., are there any backup snapshots that could retain data beyond 90 days unless explicitly requested removed)?
2) Please confirm the format of the audit export (CSV columns) and whether timestamps are in UTC.

If you can send the audit export sample and the DPA excerpt, we can run a parallel legal review.

- Claire

Claire — attaching the materials you asked for. Quick notes:
- Cold/archival backups: our standard archival tier follows the 90-day retention policy; we can add contract language that Redwood will not restore or retain customer data beyond 90 days except under a documented legal hold.
- Audit export: attached sample is CSV with columns: request_id, event_type, actor, resource_id, region, timestamp_utc, task_id, status. Timestamps are in UTC.
- DPA excerpt: highlighted deletion & backup clauses; we can prepare a DPA amendment that switches backup retention to 30 days for Aquila if you confirm via signed addendum.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_excerpt_2027.pdf, retention_matrix_2027.xlsx, sample-audit-log-export.txt

Please confirm next steps and whether you want Neha to prepare the redlined DPA language for the 30-day backup option.

Thanks,
Diego
